plants.name: Prunus × yedoensis
plants.description: A deciduous tree that produces abundant clusters of delicate, fragrant, five-petaled blossoms before its leaves emerge, creating a cloud-like canopy of pale flowers. It is the most famous ornamental cherry in Japan and is widely planted in parks and along rivers.
plants.location: Japan, Washington D.C. (USA), South Korea, and temperate regions of the Northern Hemisphere
plants.funFact: The Yoshino cherry is the centerpiece of Japan's hanami tradition, and the Japan Meteorological Agency publishes an annual 'cherry blossom forecast' tracking the bloom front as it moves northward.

plants.name: Narcissus pseudonarcissus
plants.description: A bulbous perennial with trumpet-shaped golden flowers and paler outer petals, rising above strap-like blue-green leaves. It grows in woodlands and meadows and is the ancestor of many cultivated daffodil varieties.
plants.location: Western Europe, especially the United Kingdom, France, and Spain; naturalized in North America
plants.funFact: All parts of the daffodil contain toxic alkaloids such as lycorine, which deter grazing animals, and galantamine from related Narcissus species is used in medicine to treat symptoms of Alzheimer's disease.

plants.name: Magnolia × soulangeana
plants.description: A small deciduous tree or large shrub bearing large, goblet-shaped flowers on bare branches in early spring. The blossoms are often tinged with pink or purple at the base and are a hallmark of spring in temperate gardens.
plants.location: Cultivated across temperate Europe, the eastern and western United States, and East Asia
plants.funFact: Magnolias are among the most ancient flowering plants, having evolved before bees existed, and their flowers are thought to have been pollinated by beetles.

plants.name: Colchicum autumnale
plants.description: Despite its name, in the Southern Hemisphere this bulb flowers in autumn, when its goblet-shaped, crocus-like blooms emerge leafless from the ground. Its flowers appear without foliage, which has earned it the nickname 'naked ladies'.
plants.bloomingSeason: March to April in the Southern Hemisphere (autumn); September to October in the Northern Hemisphere
plants.location: Cultivated in Australia, New Zealand, and South Africa; native to Europe
plants.funFact: This plant is the source of colchicine, a compound used to treat gout and also used by plant breeders to induce chromosome doubling in crops.
